 Tribunal At Bengaluru

 Bengaluru.

Petitioner: Suresha,
 S/o Shivanna,
 Aged about 46 years,
 R/at Kodinagasandra,

 Tumakuru District.

 Major, R/o Sorvanahalli,
 Mayasandra, Turuvekere Taluk,
 Tumakuru District.

 (By Smt. H.V. Vasanthalakshmi,
 Advocate)
 2.

United India Insurance Co. Ltd.,
 Regional Office, T.P. Hub,
 5th and 6th floors, Krishi Bhavan,
 Hudson Circle, Opp.
BBMP Head  Office, Nrupathunga Road,
SCCH-1 2 MVC No.5852/2022  Bengaluru - 560001.

(By Sri Shivakumar M.V., Advocate)
 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation from the respondents who are the owner and insurer of the Motorcycle Suresha vs Arun Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131489297/
1 bearing No.KA-44-S-0274 asserting that on 20.07.2022 at about 1.15 p.m. when riding a TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA-44-L-9037 by keep sitting his wife Shashikala on the pillion, on NH-150(a)
T.B. Cross, towards Mayasandra, Turuvekere Taluk, near HP Petrol bunk, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274, rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the rear part of the moped, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.

2. Petitioner took treatment at Government hospital, Mayasandra and Adichunchanagiri Hospital,
B.G. Nagara, as on the date of accident petitioner being aged about 46 years, used to earn Rs.30,000/-p.m. by vending vegetables and fruits.

3. Regarding accident Turuvekere police registered crime No.165/2022 against the rider of the Motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274.
4.
In response to the notice respondent No.1 - owner of the motorcycle appeared through his advocate, but neither filed written statement nor participated in the proceedings.

5. In response to the notice respondent No.2- insurance company appeared through his Advocate and filed written statement denying the reason and mode of accident nature and consequences of injuries suffered by petitioner.

In para No.5 of the additional written statement respondent No.2-insurance company denied the liability to indemnify the respondent No.1 on the ground that Abhi @ Abhishek rode Bike bearing No. KA-44-S-0274 without driving licence.

6. On the basis of the pleadings on 25.04.2023, this Authority has framed the following issues :
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 20.07.2022 at about 1.15 p.m. near HP petrol bunk, NH-150(A) road, Mayasandra, Turuvekere Taluk, Tumakuru District, he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the rider of the Bajaj Puslar Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-44-S-0274 as alleged?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled to compensation ? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
7. On 22.07.2024, 05.08.2024, 24.01.2025 petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 9 documents at Ex.P.1 to P.9.
On 25.09.2024, 14.02.2025 petitioner produced the evidence of MRO at Adichunchanagiri Hospital and Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2 and PW3 and get produced 6 documents at Ex.P.10 to P.15.

On 11.03.2025, 14.03.2025 the respondent No.2-insurance company produced the evidence of officer as RW1 and produced 4 documents at Ex.R1 to Ex.R.4.
8.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the records.

2 9.

On the basis of the record, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2 ...

Petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.2,14,045/-
with current and future interest at 6% p.a. as compensation.
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner stated that on 20.07.2022 at about 1.15 p.m. when riding a TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA-44-L-9037 by keep sitting his wife Shashikala on the pillion, on NH-150(a) T.B. Cross, towards Mayasandra, Turuvekere Taluk, near HP Petrol bunk, rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274, rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the rear part of the moped, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
11. In the written statement respondent No. 2 denied the allegation regarding reason and mode of the accident.

12. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that regarding the accident his wife Shashikala filed complaint and immediately after the accident he has been shifted to Government Hospital,
Mayasandra wherein he informed the reason for the injuries and mode of the accident.

In the cross-examination PW1 denied the suggestion that he rode the moped by keep sitting his wife on the pillion, lost balance, fell along with moped, suffered injuries, therefore after 7 days filed a false complaint against the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-44-S-0274.
Petitioner stated that in the accident his wife suffered simple injuries.

13. In the evidence PW2-MRO - Adichunchanagiri Hospital produced MLC extract and police intimation copy at Ex.P11 and P.12.
14.
In the evidence PW3- Dr. Nagaraj B.N. stated nothing about the reason and mode of the accident.

15. In the evidence affidavit RW1 - officer of the insurance company stated about violation of the terms of the policy by the insured of the motorcycle bearing No. KA- 44-S-0274.
16.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR and complaint pertaining to crime No.165/2022 registered by Turuvekere police on 27.07.2022 against the rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337 of IPC regarding accident taken place between Motorcycle bearing No.KA- 44-S-0274 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-L-9037 on 20.07.2022 resulting in the injuries to petitioner on the basis of the complaint presented by Shashikala wife of the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of spot mahazar.

Ex.P.3 is the copy of wound Suresha vs Arun Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131489297/
3 certificate in which reason for the injuries are noted as RTA near Mayasandra petrol bunk, at 1.00 p.m. 20.07.2022 between 2 bikes.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of Accident inspection report.

Ex.P.5 is the copy of the charge sheet filed by Turuvekere police in crime No.165/2022 against Abhi @ Abhishek C.B.
S/o Balagangadharagowda C.K. - rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,337, 338 of IPC and Sec.181 of MV Act.

In the MLC extract marked at Ex.P.11 appearance of the petitioner with injuries alleged to have been suffered in RTA collision between pulsar bike and TVS Heavy duty at Mayasandra, near Petrol bunk, at about 1.00 p.m. on 20.07.2022, initially treated at PHC, Mayasandra and referred are mentioned.

Ex.P.12 is the intimation forwarded by the doctors of Adichunchanagiri hospital to PSI, Belluru police station intimating appearance of the petitioner on 20.07.2022 with the history of RTA collision between pulsar V/s TVS heavy duty.
17. In this case there are no reasons to disbelieve the evidence of petitioner and contents of the police records regarding the reason, mode and consequence of the accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 20.07.2022 at about 1.15 p.m. when petitioner was riding a TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA-44-L-9037 by keep sitting his wife Shashikala on the pillion, on NH-150(a) T.B.
Cross, towards Mayasandra, Turuvekere Taluk, near HP Petrol bunk, Abi @ Abishek- rider of Motorcycle bearing No.KA- 44-S-0274, rode the same negligently, dashed the same to the rear part of the moped, thereby caused accident, caused injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered closed displaced middle 1/3 fracture of right clavicle, took first aid at Mayasandra Government Hospital, then took treatment at Adichunchanagiri hospital, B.G. Nagara as inpatient from 20.07.2022 to 03.08.2022 underwent surgery by spending Rs.1,00,000/-, as on the date of accident used to earn Rs.30,000/-p.m. by vending vegetables and fruits.
19. In the written statement, respondent No.2 denied the allegation regarding nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

20. In the cross-examination PW.1 stated about taking of treatment at Adichunchanagiri Hospital,
Bellur for a period of 15 days.
PW1 denied the suggestion about non-spending of Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment.

21. In the evidence PW2-MRO produced the inpatient record at Ex.P.13.
22.

In the evidence PW.3- Dr. Nagaraj B.N. Orthopedic Surgeon stated that on 24.01.2025 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered permanent physical disability at 30% to right arm which is about 10% to the whole body.
In the evidence PW.3 produced OPD card dated 24.01.2025 and X-rays at Ex.P.14 and P.15.
In the cross-examination PW.3 submitted that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified inpatient treatment record of the petitioner.
PW.3 stated that as on 24.01.2025 clavicle fracture of petitioner was united.
PW3 submitted ignorance about the avocation of the petitioner.

Suresha vs Arun Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131489297/
4 23.
In the evidence RW1- officer of the insurance company stated nothing regarding nature and consequences of the injuries suffered by the petitioner 24.

Wound certificate, Discharge summary, medical bills, case files, X-ray and other medical records shows that in the accident petitioner suffered closed displaced middle 1/3 fracture of right clavicle,
took first aid at Mayasandra Government Hospital, then took treatment at Adichunchanagiri hospital, B.G. Nagara as inpatient from 20.07.2022 to 03.08.2022.
25.
In the Aadhaar card marked at Ex.P.7 the birth year of the petitioner is noted as 1976.
The medical bills shows that petitioner approximately spent Rs.21,545/- for treatment.
In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence regarding his occupation and quantum of income.
In this case petitioner has not produced any evidence to show either decrease in the income or loss of income subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence,
I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW.3 Dr.Nagaraj B.N. is not sufficient to award compensation under the head loss of future income(Permanent functional Disability).

26. Considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place and nature of treatment taken by the petitioner, lack of documentary evidence regarding occupation and income of the petitioner, I award Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.21,545/- towards medical expenses, Rs.20,000/- towards attendant conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.77,500/-
(15,500 x5) towards loss of income during treatment period and Rs.45,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.
27.
Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for Rs.2,14,045/- with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the respondents as compensation.
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs 1.
Pain and sufferings 60,000-00 2.

Medical expenses 21,545-00 3. Attendant conveyance and 20,000-00 nourishment charges 4. Loss of income during 77,500-00 treatment period 5. Loss of amenities and future 45,000-00 unhappiness Total 2,14,045-00
Hence, I answer Issue No.2 accordingly.

28. Issue No.3: On 08.04.2025 learned advocate appearing for the petitioner filed copy of the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka passed in MFA 202104/2024 (MV-D) dated 19.09.2024 - Branch Manager, ICICI Lombard GIC V/s Pooja & others and judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Alhabhad passed in First Appeal No.1780/2024 dated 31.01.2025- ICICI Lombard GIC v/s Arti Devi & others requested to direct the insurance company to deposit the compensation Suresha vs Arun Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131489297/
5 amount then to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle in case of violation of the terms of the policy.

sentences.text: In the light of the judgments cited above with reference to the submission made on behalf of both the parties, I have appreciated the material available in the file.

In the evidence RW1-officer of the insurance company stated that after investigation police have filed charge sheet against Abhi @ Abhishek S/o Balagangadharagowda - rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274 for having committed offence punishable under provisions of motor vehicle Act for riding the motorcycle without licence, thereby respondent No.1 violated Sec.3 of MV Act, therefore respondent No.1 is not entitle to indemnify by respondent No.2.

In evidence RW1 produced copy of the policy,
carbon copy of the letter dated 10.07.2023 sent to respondent No.1- Arunkumar, Postal acknowledgment card bearing address/signature of respondent No.1- Arunkumar with date 15.07.2023 at Ex.R.2 to R.4.

In the cross-examination RW1 admitted that after investigation police have filed charge sheet against Abhishek C.B.- rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 44-S-0274 for having committed the offence punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC, Sec.181 of IMV Act.

The copy of the policy shows that as on the date of accident motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-44-S-0274 had insurance coverage through respondent No.2.
29.

As referred above charge sheet shows that after investigation police have filed charge sheet against Abhi @ Abhishek S/o Balagangadharagowda - rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274 for having committed offence punishable under Sec.279,337, 338 of IPC and Sec.181 of MV Act.
In this case neither the petitioner nor the respondent No.1 produced document to show that as on the date of accident Abhi @ Abhishek had licence to ride the motorcycle with gear.

30. In this case there is no explanation by respondent No.1 owner of the motorcycle or petitioner the effort if any made by the respondent No.1 to know whether Abhishek @ Abhi had licence to ride motorcycle or not.

31. In several judgments Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, various Hon'ble High Courts and Hon'ble Apex court opined that in case of violation of the driver clause of the policy the insured/owner of the vehicle is not entitle to be indemnified by the insurer.

Hence, it is clear that the respondent No.1 by authorizing Abhi @ Abhishek to ride motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274 without licence violated the driver clause of the policy, therefore, respondent No.1 owner of the motorcycle bearing No.KA- 44-S-0274 is not entitle to be indemnified from the respondent No.2- insurance company, therefore alone liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.3 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is partly allowed.

The respondent No.1 being the owner of motorcycle bearing No.KA-44-S-0274 shall pay Rs.2,14,045/- (Rupees two lakhs fourteen thousand forty five only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.

Suresha vs Arun Kumar on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131489297/
6
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.

It is clarified that petitioner/respondent No.1 are at liberty to insist the respondent No.2- insurance company to deposit the compensation amount by producing documents to show that as on the date of incident Abhi @ Abhishek S/o Balagangadharagowda had licence to ride motorcycle.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 9th day of April, 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
Bangalore.
